name: Brownism
summary: Brownism is the approach of Gordon Brown and his followers in the Labour Party, usually placed in social democracy and set against Blair's New Labour. It keeps market pragmatism, fiscal prudence and an independent central bank, while pursuing redistribution through tax credits, the New Deal and heavy health and education spending. It is internationalist on aid, debt relief and global financial regulation, cautious on the euro, and attached to a values-based Britishness.
scope: The strand represented is Gordon Brown's chancellorship (1997-2007) and premiership (2007-2010) as described by Wikipedia, Skidelsky, Coyle and a scholarly review of his economics, plus his 2008 UN speech on the world economy. It excludes Blairism's more market-driven public-service reform, and the later Brownite-Labour left. Many social-issue statements were not addressed by these sources and are answered at low confidence from mainstream Labour positions.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Brownism keeps a strong state and channelled the biggest spending rises of the Brown chancellorship into the NHS and education, so tax-funded universal care is a settled commitment.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Brown introduced the national minimum wage as part of welfare-to-work and backed a decent floor, but "substantially" raising it was not a Brownite aim, which was moderate and Low Pay Commission-led.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Brownism pairs market pragmatism and "responsible capitalism" with a strong state, so adherents would reject both the claim that markets always beat governments and its opposite.

public-ownership.rationale: Brown dropped nationalised industry and direct state investment as Old Labour tools; public ownership returned only as emergency rescue of banks in 2008.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Brown raised taxes selectively, including windfall levies and pension reliefs, but kept the 40 percent top rate as a red line, so adherents are split on significantly higher taxes on the wealthy.

unions-good.rationale: Labour's union link and the minimum wage fit a favourable view, but the sources do not discuss Brown on unions directly; inferred from Labour tradition.

property-fundamental.rationale: Not discussed in sources; a social-democratic outlook that accepts redistribution implies private property can be overridden for public purposes, inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Brown's chancellorship was light-touch on finance, but after 2008 he called for tougher regulation and global supervision, so the stance is mixed.

cut-welfare.rationale: Brownism uses tax credits and in-work benefits to fight poverty, expanding rather than cutting welfare; it frames benefits as a route to work, not as a dependency to cut.

worker-ownership.rationale: Not part of Brownite policy, which left industry in private hands; inferred from its move away from Old Labour economics.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Brown's government pushed counter-terror powers such as 42-day detention; the sources only touch the civil-liberties side lightly, so this is inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Brown's 2007 conference speech announced tougher measures on drugs and crime; legalisation was not a Brownite position (inferred).

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Mainstream Labour governments kept and extended hate-crime law; the sources do not address this for Brownism.

strong-leader.rationale: Brownism stressed constitutional reform and limiting executive power, such as war powers, over leaders bypassing gridlock.

state-harmful.rationale: Brownism is defined by a strong state and public-service expansion, so calling the state unnecessary and harmful is flatly opposed.

limit-guns.rationale: Brown pledged five years in prison for gun possession in 2007; a position on strict licensing is inferred from Labour policy.

empower-police-military.rationale: His 2007 conference speech paired a "strong Britain" with tough crime measures; inferred support for more police powers.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed in sources; Labour governments under Brown did not liberalise sex work and moved to tighten rules.

decide-locally.rationale: Brownism centralised funding and targets on public services, tying money to national targets rather than devolving decisions.

rehabilitation.rationale: His crime agenda was framed as "punish and prevent", combining both; adherents are split.

traditional-family.rationale: Brown spoke of families and responsibility but sources show no traditionalist stance; treated as split.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; mainstream Labour and its Brown government supported civil partnerships and later equal marriage.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed in sources; inferred from mainstream Labour support for legal abortion.

more-religion-public.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Brown spoke of "moral sentiments" but the Brownite programme did not seek a larger public role for religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred from a social-democratic commitment to fairness; the sources do not discuss race policy.

gender-social-construct.rationale: No source records any Brownite view on the nature of gender, which was not part of its programme.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Brown's Britishness agenda and "British values" rhetoric treated shared values and national identity as important, though Barnett found it backward-looking.

gradual-change.rationale: Brown's "prudence, stability and caution" and Skidelsky's "patient politician" portrait describe incrementalism within existing institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: "British jobs for British workers" rhetoric and the 2007 deportation proposals signal a restrictionist turn, but sources are thin.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Brown told the UN that global problems need global solutions and that post-war institutions must be updated, including global financial supervision.

free-trade.rationale: Skidelsky describes Brown as committed to globalisation and efficiency alongside fairness, which implies support for open trade.

nation-first.rationale: Brownism emphasises international cooperation, aid and multilateral action rather than putting national interest ahead of it.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Brown's foreign policy leaned on soft power and he privately doubted Iraq, but he backed Blair's government; Brownism is cautious about military intervention.

open-borders.rationale: A "stronger Britain" with British jobs for British workers is opposed to eventual open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Brownism is built on growth and rising prosperity, with the UN speech celebrating a doubling world economy.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Brown said he was committed to tackling climate change and called for tough decisions on energy and climate, though not as a drastic transformation.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed; Brown stressed skills and global cooperation more than technology.

expand-nuclear.rationale: His government backed new nuclear power for energy security; the speech only refers to hard energy choices, so inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: A cautious, parliamentary reformer, Brown stands opposed to revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: Brown delegated interest rates to the Bank of England and set fiscal rules, but also pushed public targets and democratic reform. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

central-planning.rationale: Brown rejected Old Labour tools such as direct state investment and fine-tuning, and embraced markets.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not a Brownite concern; markets are accepted regardless of ownership but worker or public ownership was not a goal.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not part of Brown's tax approach; stamp duty and indirect taxes were relied on, so replacing other taxes with a land tax is unlikely.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance tax was not a Brownite focus in the sources; adherents split.

basic-income.rationale: Brown's welfare approach stresses work and in-work benefits rather than unconditional income.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Committed to globalisation, Brownism opposes protectionist tariffs.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Brown rejected direct state investment in industry as an Old Labour tool.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Brownism neither championed wide small-ownership schemes nor opposed them; asset-based policies like Child Trust Funds exist but the sources do not frame them this way.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Brownism is committed to markets and wages; abolishing them is out of the question.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Brown gave the Bank of England operational independence in 1997, so abolishing central banks contradicts a signature reform.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The sources describe Brown abandoning Old Labour methods of state-managed economic coordination for central bank independence and fiscal rules.

one-party-rule.rationale: Brown's Governance of Britain agenda was about parliamentary accountability, opposed to one-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Brown's constitutional reforms left the monarchy untouched; support inferred.

democracy-best.rationale: Brown's constitutional renewal programme assumed parliamentary democracy as the proper form of government.

direct-votes.rationale: Barnett notes he avoided referendum demands; reform focused on Parliament.

workers-councils.rationale: Brownism is parliamentary social democracy with no support for councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: As a Scottish Labour politician who stressed unity and Britishness, Brown opposed secession.

natural-rulers.rationale: Brown's meritocratic outlook, admiring American enterprise and merit, rejects natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: Not addressed; a constitutional reformer would generally reject political violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: Skidelsky describes Brown's foreign policy as economic soft power; glorifying war does not fit.

separate-church-state.rationale: Not addressed; Brown spoke of moral values but not a position on strict separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: A British parliamentary reformer rejects laws based on scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Brownism favours a strong state, so private provision of courts and defence is rejected.

military-superiority.rationale: Brown favoured soft power but backed the nuclear deterrent and alliances; split.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Brown's Britishness defined by shared values of liberty, fairness and responsibility, not ethnicity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Skidelsky shows Brown marrying American capitalism with Scottish socialism, not Marxist class struggle.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Brown sought fairness and opportunity through human capital and work, not equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not discussed in any Brownite source; no stance can be derived from its economic and constitutional programme.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Brown favoured aid and debt relief but not reparations; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not a Brownite idea; Britain's place is in global institutions rather than civilisational blocs.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Brown's Smithian moral sentiments tradition ties markets to morality rather than celebrating self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Brown's rhetoric of responsibility and liberty balances rights and duties.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed; he focused on climate and resources as economic problems.

limit-population.rationale: Brown noted rising population as pressure on resources, but active limits were not proposed.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The UN speech celebrates growing prosperity of globalisation.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Brown's speeches focus on skills and global coordination, not on speeding technological disruption of institutions.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bioethics of this kind falls outside what the Brownite sources discuss.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a traditional parliamentary view.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from the Brown government's pursuit of extended counter-terror powers, which suggests it would favour state access over unbreakable privacy.

restore-past-order.rationale: Brown looked to a new global age and rebuilding institutions for the future, not restoring a lost order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Wikipedia says Brownism is described as lacking an ideological narrative, marked by pragmatism and responsibility.

direct-action.rationale: Brown, a patient parliamentarian per Skidelsky, pursued change through budgets, legislation and elections, not extra-parliamentary action.

means-match-ends.rationale: A question about prefigurative politics that Brownism, as a governing doctrine, never took up.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Brown's UN speech welcomes a doubling world economy and the jobs and prosperity it brings, which excludes a hunter-gatherer ideal.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Skills, training and productive work in a market economy are central to Brown's human-capital approach, which depends on specialised labour.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Brown's welfare was means-tested and work-linked, not distribution by need.

production-for-use.rationale: Brownism embraced market production for profit, with the state correcting outcomes through tax credits and public spending.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Brown celebrated entrepreneurs and enterprise; Marxist exploitation theory is rejected.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Brownism is a parliamentary social-democratic doctrine that works within elections and law, and has no equivalent of proletarian dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivised agriculture belongs to the communist tradition, and Brownism dropped even Old Labour state ownership.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Brown backed globalisation and cooperation as sources of stability.

taxation-theft.rationale: Brownism relies on taxes to fund redistribution and public services.

harm-principle.rationale: Not clearly addressed; his government restricted some liberties for security and order.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Brown's emphasis on community, responsibility and shared values balances against individual rights, but no source settles the question.

conscription.rationale: Brown's soft-power foreign policy and no record of support; inferred.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Brownism stresses democratic voting and constitutional reform.

state-as-business.rationale: Brown tied funding to targets but described public service as a social good; not a customer model.

positive-liberty.rationale: Brown's emphasis on raising human capital and fairness implies freedom needs material means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Brown's agenda treated elected government as the centre of power, and the sources show no claim that media and universities outweigh it.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Brown defined Britishness through values, rejecting race essentialism. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

organic-representation.rationale: Brown's constitutional proposals strengthened Parliament as the centre of representation, with no role for corporate or family bodies.

total-state.rationale: Brown expanded the state in health and education but kept markets, an independent central bank and private enterprise, so it was never total.

national-rebirth.rationale: Brown spoke of strong Britain but not national rebirth from decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Skidelsky describes Brown's foreign policy as economic soft power with aid and debt relief, which excludes territorial expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority in Brown's constitutional agenda rests on Parliament and law, not personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Bound labour is incompatible with a labour-market doctrine of flexible work, minimum wage and training.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Brownism's results-focused pragmatism implies knowledge and evidence can be neutral enough to judge policy, though sources do not discuss epistemology.

universal-morality.rationale: Brown's Smithian moral sentiments tradition and "global values" talk lean to universal morality.

single-common-good.rationale: Brown's pragmatic, balancing style, trading prudence against redistribution, fits a plural view of interests more than a single rational common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The sources are silent; mainstream Labour leaders including Brown have supported Israel's right to exist, so a mild agree is inferred.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: No source records a Brownite view on diaspora return rights.

revive-national-language.rationale: The question has no connection to the sources on Brownism.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not part of Brownism; he accepted flexible hiring and conventional corporate governance.

school-vouchers.rationale: Brownism favoured public provision with targets, with a more cautious view on market reforms in education.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Brown's golden rule allowed borrowing to invest, and in 2008-09 he backed fiscal stimulus and warned against withdrawing it early.

economic-freedom.rationale: Brown paired market liberalisation with strong state action, and no source says whether he saw political freedom as depending on economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Brownism's reform agenda relied on law, accountability and institutions, so ruling mainly by moral example is unlikely, though not discussed.

national-self-determination.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from liberal internationalism.

force-without-un.rationale: Brown preferred multilateral action and had misgivings about Iraq, so would prefer UN approval.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Brown's Smithian moral-sentiments thinking gives emotion a role in morality, and no source places him on this question.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: His 'British jobs for British workers' line hints at restricting access, but no source states a Brownite welfare-eligibility rule.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Brown's New Deal required the young unemployed to take work or training, tying benefits to work.

class-collaboration.rationale: Brown's growth-and-fairness synthesis and acceptance of business favoured cooperation over class conflict.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Brown's agenda valued British institutions and culture, so sacrificing libraries and museums for new creation does not fit.

dominated-front.rationale: Brown supports cooperation with all, not fronts against the West.

workers-nation.rationale: The sources record no stance on whether workers organise nationally or internationally.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Brown led a Labour government that backed gender equality in law, so legally distinct roles for men and women run against the party line.

ban-interest.rationale: Brown's chancellorship was built around monetary rules, an independent central bank and a functioning credit system, so banning interest is excluded.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Brownite Britishness rests on shared values; segregation is wholly opposed.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Skidelsky shows Brown reconciling capitalism and social aims through the state, which he saw as an instrument of fairness, not class domination.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Brown acknowledged oil's continued role but committed to climate action; inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Britishness agenda stressed shared values, but not abandonment of culture; split.

elite-replacement.rationale: The sources give no hint of conspiracy thinking; Brown's Britishness rests on shared values open to all, which contradicts the replacement claim.

proportional-representation.rationale: Brown's constitutional agenda avoided changing the voting system.

national-mission.rationale: Brown's foreign policy is cooperative and multilateral, with no claim to a special mission to export British government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not covered in the sources; mainstream Labour leaders accept structural disadvantage for women in pay and politics, so a mild agree is inferred.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Brown's 2007 reform aimed to restore trust; rejects the claim.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic policy has no place in the liberal social-democratic values Brown's Britishness is based on.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The sources do not discuss accountability for past security-force abuses; Brown's government was split on legacy inquiries.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Brown expanded spending on health and education and ran redistributive budgets, so a state limited to defence and justice is the opposite of his approach.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The statement is contrary to a Britishness built on shared values and equal worth, as described in Brown's Britishness speech.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Brown's liberty-fairness values are premised on equal worth.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A debate internal to Marxism-Leninism, and Brownism is not a revolutionary socialism; a mild disagree is inferred.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Brown's Britishness agenda rested on common values and shared citizenship, so a single civil law for everyone fits, but this is inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Brown's liberty-and-fairness values include religious freedom, so legal restrictions on conversion would be opposed.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A religiously motivated ban has no basis in Brownite economics or politics, and farming policy was never part of it.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The sources do not address it; Labour under Brown left faith schools in place and split on religious instruction.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine about socialist states that Brownism, a parliamentary party doctrine, does not share.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Brown's Governance of Britain programme was about parliamentary accountability.

trade-surplus.rationale: Brown's free-trade globalism does not treat export surpluses as a goal; Britain ran deficits under his chancellorship, but sources do not discuss the aim.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal of a minority contradicts the liberal Britishness and equal-rights outlook in Brown's speeches.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Brownism relies on taxation and state coercion for redistribution, which an absolute non-aggression rule would forbid.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Not addressed beyond enterprise; Social Darwinist form rejected.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The sources record no Brownite position on banning parties; Britain has not done so and Brown did not propose it.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: A republican theory of freedom that Brownism does not discuss in its sources.

separated-powers.rationale: Governance of Britain proposals sought to limit executive prerogative powers.

vanguard-party.rationale: Leninist vanguardism contradicts Brownism's parliamentary, electoral route to change.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Brown's budgets were redistributive toward the long-term unemployed and low-paid working families, ending child poverty.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Labour accepted Right to Buy after 1997, but the sources do not record Brown's own view.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Not addressed; New Labour kept Thatcher-era restrictions in place.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Rejected; Brown saw poverty as an institutional and human-capital issue.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Brown's Britishness speech presents shared values, not homogeneity, as the basis of cohesion.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Brown's constitutional reform sought to strengthen elected Parliament, so replacing elections by lottery is opposed.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Brownism sought constitutional safeguards, though he pursued extended detention; mild disagree.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Brownism abandoned direct state controls in favour of market mechanisms, though emergency support for energy bills in 2008 shows some flexibility.

party-controls-media.rationale: A multi-party parliamentary democrat who pushed openness would reject government control of media.

party-commands-army.rationale: Brown proposed giving Parliament a bigger say over war powers, the opposite of a ruling party commanding the army.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: His government introduced an 'earned citizenship' idea, but the sources record no firm Brownite position, so adherents are split.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Brownism accepts market pay and rewards for talent, and nothing suggests capping MPs at an average wage.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Brown ran a disciplined party, but the sources do not frame a binding-decisions doctrine.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Brown was consistently Eurosceptic on the euro and unwilling to give up his fiscal rules.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The Governance of Britain green paper proposed curbing the prerogative power of executive to commit troops, which opposes unchecked executive command.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The sources record no view on how churches should be governed; Brown, a son of the manse, left church governance to churches.

clerical-rule.rationale: Brownism rests on parliamentary democracy and gives no authority to clerics.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Skidelsky describes Brown as unwilling to oppose his own government over Iraq, which excludes a revolutionary defeatist position.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: A liberal social-democratic government has no programme of moral censorship of art.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: A question about presidents that does not apply to a parliamentary system; not discussed in sources.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of MPs was debated after the 2009 expenses scandal under Brown, but the sources record no Brownite stance.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Skidelsky describes Brown as at home with America; he valued alliances.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Brownism is a mixed-economy outlook that accepts private and social renting, and compulsory ownership has no source.

people-in-arms.rationale: Skidelsky's account of Brown's alliance-based, professional-armed-force foreign policy leaves no room for an armed citizenry replacing the army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The sources show no sign of rural romanticism; Brown's economics focuses on urban, industrial, services-based prosperity.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Not covered; the question is about Korea or Ireland-type cases on which Brownite sources are silent.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Brown made education a core theme of his 2007 conference speech.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Brown's Britishness stressed shared values and some cultural hierarchy of values, but he made no statement on comparing cultures.

death-penalty.rationale: Britain abolished it; Labour governments rejected its return.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Brown's emphasis on education as a core theme and mainstream Labour policy makes this a likely agree, though inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: An evidence-based pragmatist and education-focused government would not teach creationism in public schools.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The sources record no Brownite stance; Labour governments split between liberty and restriction.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Brown defined Britishness through values and proposed an earned citizenship route, not descent.

minority-language-support.rationale: Brown backed Scottish devolution, but no source records his view on minority languages.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: A Millian theme not addressed by any Brownite source.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Skidelsky notes Brown backed G7 debt relief in 1999 for poor countries.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Brown's approach to poor-country independence was integration and aid, not wholesale change of the property system.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The Governance of Britain agenda was piecemeal reform of existing institutions rather than a new constitution by a constituent assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Brown's own reform agenda sought more accountable government, so trading freedoms for growth is out of line.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Skidelsky documents Brown's push for rising aid, G7 debt relief and compacts to fund health and education in poor countries.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Brown's government renewed Trident; not covered in sources, inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Brown left the monarchy intact in his constitutional proposals.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Brown gave the Bank of England operational independence over interest rates in 1997.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Mainstream Labour backs a land-for-peace settlement in the Middle East; this is inferred and not source-stated.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Brownite redistribution and windfall levies imply property rights yield to public purposes, but sources do not state the principle directly.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A debate inside the Marxist left that Brownism did not engage.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Brown's UN speech calls for action on climate and energy, but the sources do not say if he applied a precautionary principle.

collective-defense.rationale: Skidelsky's account of Brown's Atlanticism supports alliance commitments.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Brown's UN speech argues for a rules-based international order, from which a view that annexation without consent is unlawful would follow, though no source applies this to a case.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The sources record no stance, and a Brown government with a moral-values tone did not seek to curb churches.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Brown's constitutional agenda kept a hereditary monarchy above party politics, so he implicitly accepts a non-partisan head of state.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Brown opposed Scottish independence politically, but no source says he would use force to stop secession.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The one-country-two-systems idea is not discussed in any Brownite source.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A secular parliamentary politician does not hold a sacred or divine view of the head of state.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Brown ran progressive taxes and targeted tax credits for low-paid families, the opposite of a flat tax.

character-from-environment.rationale: Brown's investment in human capital assumes circumstances and training form people.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Brown's Governance of Britain agenda sought to limit executive prerogative powers, so a ruler above the law is opposed.

space-expansion.rationale: The sources show no interest in space; Brown's priorities are economic and social.

mixed-constitution.rationale: His reforms included Lords reform, but no source frames the constitution as mixing few and many.

leader-cult.rationale: Brown's constitutional agenda sought less personal executive power and no cult of the leader.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist idea outside the parliamentary Brownite tradition.

land-redistribution.rationale: Seizing large estates is outside Brownism, which works through taxation and spending rather than expropriation.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Brown's liberal internationalism and rule-based order exclude claiming territory because co-nationals live there.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Brown's liberty-and-fairness values include freedom of belief, so punishing apostasy is opposed.

women-must-cover.rationale: A Labour government committed to equality and civil liberties would reject legally mandated coverings.

common-currency.rationale: Skidelsky: Brown consistently resisted joining the euro, keeping his monetary and fiscal rules.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Brown's internationalism is global and institution-based, not tied to ancestry or language families.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: A question from Central European minority politics that Brownite sources do not touch.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Brown's Britishness of shared citizenship and equal rights implies minorities should seek equality where they live, but this is inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Brown's Smithian moral outlook rather than historical materialism.

ban-cartels.rationale: New Labour strengthened competition law, and Brown's idea of fair rules fits a pro-competition stance, though sources do not state it.

no-bailouts.rationale: Brown's government nationalised and bailed out RBS, Lloyds and Northern Rock, and urged other countries to follow.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Brown's agenda strengthened checks and accountability on the executive, which sits against majority supremacy over courts.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Labour used all-women shortlists, but no source records Brown's view on mandatory parity in public bodies.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Skidelsky describes Brown as committed to globalisation, which excludes a closed economic bloc.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Brown asked for global rules on finance and energy, but no source states his view on labour and environmental clauses in trade agreements.

moral-incentives.rationale: Coyle notes Brown backed large entrepreneurial rewards, which is material incentive, not moral incentive.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Skidelsky's picture of a patient parliamentary politician is incompatible with insurrectionary tactics.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Brown's Governance of Britain agenda included Lords reform, continuing Labour's removal of hereditary peers, though he did not touch the monarchy.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Brown's Britishness agenda favoured teaching British history, but whether it should be central is not stated.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Skidelsky's account of Brown's aid and debt relief approach treats poor countries as partners, not wards.

patriotic-education.rationale: Brown promoted Britishness but sources do not show school patriotism.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Labour opposed quotas in Britain, but the sources do not discuss racial preferences, so only a mild disagree is inferred.

public-money-creation.rationale: Brown reinforced the independent central bank's role but left credit creation to private banks, so public-only money creation is not his position.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Brown's synthesis of market capitalism with state support, and his response to the 2008 crisis through intervention, treat capitalism as reformable rather than collapsing.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The sources do not say whether Brownism cultivates ties with former colonies; Brown's Commonwealth and aid links make this a loose split.

delink-world-market.rationale: Brownism is committed to globalisation and wants poor countries integrated through aid and debt relief, not delinked.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Brown held that rich-country workers gain from globalisation by raising skills, and no Leninist exploitation theory sits behind this.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: A social-democratic party that legislated for equality would reject a licence to discriminate.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Governance of Britain agenda explored a British bill of rights and duties, but sources give no firm Brownite line on entrenchment.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not covered by any source on Brownism.

elective-rulers.rationale: Brown's constitutional agenda accepted the monarchy, but he supported electing government via Parliament; low confidence on the monarchy part.

minority-veto.rationale: Brownism works through majoritarian parliamentary government, with no veto for dissenting members.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Not addressed; a classical liberal theme absent from the sources.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The Governance of Britain agenda aimed to strengthen Parliament against the prerogative, including over war powers.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not covered by sources; mainstream centre-left view inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not covered by sources; mainstream centre-left view inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Brown's Scottish moral-sentiments outlook stresses responsibility but sources do not frame it as an elite duty.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Brown was a lifelong political activist who sought to mobilise citizens in public life, so he would reject withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A Frankfurt School idea absent from Brownism, whose moral outlook comes from Adam Smith.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian analysis is not part of Brownism, though his early Scottish socialism may have touched it.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Brownism sees globalisation as an opportunity, with aid and debt relief as corrective, not an extraction system.

native-born-offices.rationale: Not part of Brownism, whose Britishness is about shared values, not birthplace.

party-own-road.rationale: A debate within the communist movement with no Brownite position.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Brown pushed rising aid, debt relief and funding compacts for poor countries.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Not addressed; a liberal internationalist would reject revanchism.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Brown's democratic equality of citizens regardless of descent implies opposing inherited leadership by one group.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The sources record no stance on constitutional anti-fascism, which is a continental question.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Brownite sources do not take up the totalitarianism comparison.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not covered by sources; mainstream historical view assumed.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Labour government services focused on female victims; sources do not address symmetry directly.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Brown's UN speech assumed common global principles for institutions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Brown's constitutional agenda placed war powers under Parliament, not the military.

paid-care-work.rationale: No Brownite source covers paid care work, though tax credits and childcare support point mildly toward valuing it.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not addressed; Brownite meritocracy but elected office is the norm.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Committed to globalisation and open capital, he would resist blocking takeovers broadly.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not covered in sources; mainstream Labour position inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Brown's parliamentary approach has MPs act as representatives, not mandated delegates.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Brown's pension reforms favoured state minimum guarantees and pension credit.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Brownism accepts private property and markets, and Brown abandoned Old Labour's nationalising instruments, so community-owned land with use-based tenure runs against it.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: His constitutional agenda was to strengthen parliamentary accountability.

single-official-language.rationale: Brown supported Scottish devolution and a plural Britain, so exclusive language policy is unlikely, but not addressed.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Skidelsky's account of Brown's commitment to globalisation and open capital makes a ban on foreign land ownership unlikely.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The sources do not address outcome-based discrimination tests.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Brown celebrated growth and enterprise, and sources do not show a critique of consumption.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Skidelsky describes Brown's foreign policy as soft power, so arming insurgents is unlikely.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: A Soviet-style doctrine opposed by Brown's soft-power and multilateral foreign policy.

corporate-influence.rationale: Brown courted business and finance, but post-crisis he criticised irresponsibility; split.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Brown's openness to global capital and civil society suggests unease with such limits, but this is inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Child benefit and tax credits aid families but are anti-poverty tools, not pronatalist.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not covered; a national party stressing UK-wide markets would resist local residency rules.

job-guarantee.rationale: The New Deal gave the young unemployed a job, training or study place, but it was conditional and not a universal guarantee.

democratic-peace.rationale: Not stated, but his liberal internationalism is consistent with it.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Brown's constitutional agenda assumes legitimate law, so a general lack of duty to obey is unlikely.

non-intervention.rationale: Brown backed intervention and international cooperation on debt and development, rejecting absolute non-intervention.

industrial-unions.rationale: The structure of unions is not addressed in Brownite sources.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: A conspiracy view opposed to Brownite Britishness based on shared values.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Brown's tax credits and family policy assume marriage and families as institutions, and nothing suggests abolition.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Brown's Governance of Britain agenda emphasised openness and accountability, which supports freedom of information, though specifics are not in the sources.

local-production.rationale: Skidelsky shows Brown committed to globalisation, which contradicts a preference for local production.

informal-organisation.rationale: Brown's career was in a mass party and union movement, so informal small-group politics is contrary to him.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Brown's internationalism, with global institutions, implies the contrary.

religious-nation.rationale: Brown's Britishness is defined through liberty, fairness and responsibility, not religion.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Brown's UN speech calls for cooperative international institutions among equals, not ritual tribute to a leading power.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: As a Scottish unionist who redistributed across the UK, Brown would not favour regional retention.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: A communist-theory formula not discussed by Brownite sources.

defeat-communism.rationale: Brown's career was post-Cold War, and sources give no view on this question.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Brownism is described as less enthusiastic than Blair about foundation hospitals and tuition fees, so it resisted marketising public services.

religion-illusion.rationale: Brown's moral-sentiments tradition does not treat religion as illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Brown admired enterprise and market capitalism as a base for growth.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The sources do not tie women's equality to transforming the economic system.

socialized-care.rationale: Tax credits and childcare support suggest some public role, but no source states socialising housework as a goal.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism has no place in a cosmopolitan Britishness.

treaties-binding.rationale: No Brownite source covers treaties with domestic nations.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Brownism is a mainstream party doctrine, not communitarian utopianism.

majority-settlement.rationale: Directed settlement to dilute minority regions contradicts the equal-rights Britishness Brown set out.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Brownism is a version of market capitalism with a strong state.

holocaust-denial.rationale: No mainstream British politician holds this; Brown's values-based Britishness is opposed to it, though no source addresses it directly.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Labour governments decriminalised and extended equality for gay people, so criminalisation is opposed.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Brown's constitutional renewal agenda assumed open parliamentary opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Blasphemy law was abolished under Labour in 2008, and a liberal Brownite outlook opposes punishing it.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Skidelsky's account of Brown's aid and debt relief policy is the reverse of governing territories for the ruling country's benefit.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A religious-law question to which Brownism has no connection.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Brownism rests on parliamentary legitimacy and rejects violent removal of rulers on religious grounds.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Constitutional renewal sought some citizen involvement but sources show no strong stance.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: No Brownite source addresses intersectional theory.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not covered in the sources; Labour supported the Gender Recognition Act under Blair, so a mild agree is inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: A conscience issue in Labour, and no Brownite source takes a side.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Brownism is positioned within social democracy, distinct from Blair's centrism.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept absent from Brownism, though Brown's early Scottish socialism may have touched it.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Brown's inclusive Britishness of shared values contradicts the claim of incompatibility.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Brown's Governance of Britain agenda rests authority on Parliament and accountable government, with no appeal to divine sanction.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The sources record no Brownite position on religious dress; British Labour governments left it largely to institutions, so adherents are split.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not covered in the sources; a centre-left Labour government would likely back protection for harassment complainants, so a mild inferred agree.

social-market-economy.rationale: Brownism combines market pragmatism and responsible capitalism with strong social protection and fair rules.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Brown was a committed Atlanticist who valued alliances and the armed forces' role.

rich-first.rationale: Brown's growth-and-fairness synthesis tolerates uneven gains but insists on redistribution, so adherents split.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Skidelsky calls Brown at home in America, so neutrality between blocs is contrary to him.

dynastic-succession.rationale: His constitutional agenda left the monarchy as it was and did not address leaders' succession.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Brown's chancellorship relied on conventional banking and an independent central bank, not mutual credit banks.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Brown backed global institutions and debt relief tied to development compacts.

property-franchise.rationale: Property-based franchise runs against Brown's democratic reform agenda.

domination-women-nature.rationale: An ecofeminist idea not addressed in Brownite sources.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept absent from Brownism, which accepts market economy as an organising principle.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Brownite sources do not claim press freedom is empty because of wealth.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The Governance of Britain agenda assumed law-bound government, though the sources do not state this principle.

racial-franchise.rationale: Brown's Britishness is open to all citizens, so a racial franchise is opposed.

online-participation.rationale: No Brownite source takes up online democracy.

open-government-data.rationale: Brown's openness and accountability agenda supports publishing records, though not specifically citizen proposals.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Liberal rights and equality in Brown's values rule out legal limits on interfaith marriage. No cited source addresses this statement directly.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Targeted boycotts of a religious minority contradict Brown's inclusive Britishness.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Brown's Governance of Britain agenda mentioned citizens' juries, but no source states a Brownite stance on assemblies deciding public questions.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: No Brownite source addresses religious doctrine.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Brown criticised excess in finance but welcomed entrepreneurial reward.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Labour lifted the ban in 1999, and the Brown government kept to it, though the sources do not discuss it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: A liberal democrat with a moral-values tone would not promote atheism through schools.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Brown's 2007 conference speech announced tougher crime measures, including five years in jail for gun possession.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The sources do not address consociational arrangements, though Brown supported the Northern Ireland settlement.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Brownism's core idea is expanded state action against poverty, via tax credits and public services.

term-limits.rationale: British parliamentary tradition has no term limits, and Brown did not propose them.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is outside the Brownite reform agenda, which kept representative government.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Brown's UN speech names financial and resource crises as global priorities but not extinction risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not addressed in Brownite sources, and Labour would leave religious governance to churches.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Not covered in sources; mainstream equal-marriage view inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: No Brownite source addresses it; Labour was split.

rent-control.rationale: Brownism's market pragmatism and light regulation suggest no rent caps, though sources do not discuss housing.

abolish-ip.rationale: Brown's growth model depended on enterprise and innovation, supported by conventional intellectual property rules.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Drilled national youth movements are alien to a liberal Labour programme.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Brown's government kept the Trident base at Faslane, though no source states his view.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Skidelsky's picture of Brown as Atlanticist suggests that hosting allied bases was acceptable.

recognise-genocide.rationale: No Brownite source covers genocide recognition.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Brown hit windfall profits but backed entrepreneurial rewards.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Brown supported military action by allies and accepted defensive force, contradicting absolute pacifism.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Brown's Britishness is based on values that evolve, not an unbroken ancient lineage.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: No Brownite source covers this academic question.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: No Brownite source covers feminist theory of this sort.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The sources show no martyr cult; his Britishness uses civic values rather than sacrifice rhetoric.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Brownism is described as pragmatic and lacking an ideological narrative, not a cosmic struggle.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: A Zionism-debate question outside Brownite sources.

culture-before-state.rationale: Brown's agenda was institutional and economic reform, not cultural renewal ahead of state-building.

god-not-male.rationale: Theology of this kind has no connection to Brownism in any source, so it is treated as no position.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: A feminist theology question that Brownism, a party-political economic doctrine, never addresses.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Brown's open market and Britishness of shared values oppose reserving economic life for the majority group.

independent-unions.rationale: Brown's minimum wage and employment policy worked within an independent union movement tied to Labour, though sources do not state this.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The Brownite approach accepts markets and capital with state support and does not make workers' political power a test of socialism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Brown dropped Old Labour public ownership, but the sources do not cover local water or transport.

second-chamber.rationale: Lords reform sought a reformed second chamber.

municipal-property.rationale: Brownism rejects community ownership of production; it works with private firms and national policy.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Brown's agenda centred on Westminster Parliament and unitary British government, not confederal municipal assemblies.

family-wage.rationale: Brown's tax credits top up low wages instead of requiring wages to support a family, so adherents are split.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: No Brownite source covers regulatory speed.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Brown's call for transparency and global financial supervision suggests wariness of untraceable payments.

online-anonymity.rationale: His government's counter-terror stance suggests wariness of anonymity, but the sources do not address online anonymity.

person-over-state.rationale: The sources do not state a personalist principle; Brown's emphasis on both fairness and community balances this.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Brown's Scottish moral-sentiments background touches on morality, but the sources do not state a spiritual view of politics.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Brown backed Scottish devolution within a sovereign Westminster Parliament, which can in principle revoke devolved powers.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Racial political organisation contradicts Brown's civic Britishness.

racial-pride.rationale: The sources do not cover it, but his civic Britishness stresses shared values over racial identity.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Brown, according to Skidelsky, accepted Blair's wars despite doubts, which shows tolerance of non-defensive action.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Brown's Britishness is defined by shared values across languages and religions, not language.

communal-electorates.rationale: Separate religious electorates contradict Brown's single civic Britishness.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Conspiracy thinking about partition has no place in the Brownite sources.

free-public-college.rationale: Brownism is described as less enthusiastic about tuition fees than Blair but did not move to abolish them.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Brown called for tough decisions on energy and climate, and market-based climate policy fits his approach, though specific taxes are not in the sources.

future-generations.rationale: His UN speech links energy, resource and climate decisions to long-term stability for coming generations.

arms-reduction.rationale: No Brownite source addresses it; Brown kept Trident but backed multilateral action.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Brown's UN speech favours transparency in finance, but no source addresses secret treaties.

capital-controls.rationale: The OpenEdition article says Brown gave a free hand to international capital, which is the opposite of capital controls.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Brown legislated a golden rule and a debt ceiling as the core of his economic credibility, and Coyle describes the rule that borrowing is only for investment.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Coyle documents money going to low-paid working families through tax credits as a central redistributive tool of Brown's budgets.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from mainstream Labour support for a state monopoly of force.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Not addressed; Brown backed the armed forces and a state-run defence policy, so refusing orders in interstate wars was not a Brownite position (inferred).

collective-bargaining.rationale: Brown backed union recognition and a minimum wage but kept the existing labour-law settlement, so he favoured bargaining as a norm without making it a central aim (inferred).

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Brown's UN speech and record on debt relief and aid argued for reforming global financial rules to help the poorest countries, though within the existing institutions rather than a wholesale restructuring.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Brownism is a reformist social democracy that uses the state, especially the Treasury, as its main instrument, so replacing the state machinery is far outside it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Brown's approach rested on a defined framework of fiscal rules, an independent central bank and state redistribution rather than open-ended community experiments (inferred).

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not covered by the sources opened; inferred from Brown's market-pragmatic, pro-carbon-pricing climate stance as chancellor and prime minister.

sacred-nation.rationale: Brown stressed a values-based Britishness, but a civic, shared-values patriotism is not the same as treating the nation as a sacred community (inferred).

student-debt-relief.rationale: Fiscal prudence and the retention of tuition fees point away from cancelling graduate debt; not directly addressed (inferred).

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not addressed; Brown defended the Union and addressed regional inequality through redistribution, not by describing it as colonial exploitation (inferred).

shared-human-nature.rationale: Not directly addressed; Brown's appeals to shared global responsibility and universal rights in the UN speech imply a common humanity (inferred).

public-service-media.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; mainstream Labour supported a licence-fee-funded BBC, so this is inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Not a Brownite concern; a values-based Labour politics is indifferent to the metaphysics of religion, inferred from the sources' silence.

farm-price-support.rationale: Brownism's market pragmatism favours reforming rather than expanding price guarantees; inferred from its market pragmatism, not from a farm-policy source.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The Brown government renewed Trident in 2007; inferred from mainstream Labour defence policy, not the sources read.

workers-own-party.rationale: Brownism sits inside the Labour Party, founded as the party of working people; inferred from that, though Labour is itself an established party.

ban-fgm.rationale: Mainstream Labour supports the legal ban; inferred, the sources do not address it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Equal property rights for women are mainstream Labour social-democratic doctrine; inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed; no Brownite position on language naming.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Brownism pursues policy through regulation and public spending rather than private tort remedies; inferred from its state-centred approach.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: A modernising, parliamentary Labour tradition has no place for customary chiefs in lawmaking; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Brown's government passed climate legislation but kept growth and market pragmatism central; adherents are split, inferred.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Labour governments under Blair and Brown introduced minimum sentences for repeat offenders; inferred from that record.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Brown's values-based Britishness and earned-citizenship approach favour English-language requirements; inferred from that emphasis.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Not addressed; Brown's Labour kept union recognition rights and the minimum wage and did not move to weaken union membership.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from mainstream Labour positions that stress access to voting.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Brown's values-based, inclusive Britishness and mainstream Labour positions.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred from Brown's active-state view and his Governance of Britain agenda, which treat democracy as more than elections.

premarital-sex.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from mainstream Labour social liberalism.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from mainstream Labour civil-liberties positions.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Brown extended means-tested tax credits and the New Deal on top of welfare rather than replacing welfare with a single cash payment.

women-suffrage.rationale: Equal political rights are a basic assumption of mainstream Labour social democracy and Brown's values-based approach.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from mainstream Labour positions, which place women's disadvantage in economic and social policy rather than religion.

race-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from mainstream Labour anti-racism.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Labour's support for equality machinery and Brown's redistributive, active-state approach.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from social-democratic redistribution and an active state; first-come ownership of land is not a Brownite idea.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Brown's internationalism, with global cooperation in his UN speech, suggests support for international accountability; inferred, not stated.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Brownism is a secular-pragmatic Labour approach with no scriptural literalism; inferred from mainstream Labour positions.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from mainstream Labour support for gender equality; the sources do not discuss self-government arrangements.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Brownism rejected Old Labour's state-planning tools in favour of markets and fiscal rules, so defending a planned state is inferred as rejected.

indirect-election.rationale: Brown's Governance of Britain agenda favoured direct democratic accountability; indirect delegate election is inferred as disliked.

national-church-status.rationale: Brown avoided constitutional hot potatoes such as church establishment, so Brownism is inferred as neutral.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Brown was a committed unionist who accepted existing devolution but avoided new constitutional change; inferred as neutral.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Brown's government accepted referendums on devolution and self-determination in principle; inferred at low confidence.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Brownism's internationalism and respect for the existing state order suggest keeping inherited borders; inferred.

simple-living.rationale: Brownism pursues growth and consumption-funded redistribution, so simple living is not a goal; inferred.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from mainstream Labour openness to settlement and mobility; the sources do not address indigenous regions.

equal-conscription.rationale: No documented position; inferred as neutral since the issue was not part of Brownite politics.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Brownism has a values-based Britishness but the sources do not describe a spiritual bond with land, and it is a civic idea of nation.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Brown's government kept to human-rights norms and the rule of law, and the sources show nothing resembling extrajudicial killing.

close-ties-china.rationale: The sources describe Brown as Atlanticist and prudent but give no stance on China ties, so this is not addressed.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from Brown's civic Britishness and internationalism, which do not stress kin minorities abroad.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred: Brownism keeps market pragmatism and rejected Old Labour ownership tools, so it does not hold this Georgist idea, but the sources do not address it.

self-ownership.rationale: The sources do not address self-ownership, and Brown's moral ideas stress community and duty as well as rights.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred: Brown relied on taxes on consumption such as VAT and fiscal prudence, so abolishing them is unlikely.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Brown's tax credits were targeted at low earners, but his health and education spending was universal, so the statement as a general principle is rejected only mildly.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Brown's Brownism is attached to institutions, the Governance of Britain agenda and Parliament, and he did not seek to bypass parties.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Brown backed an active state and rewards for enterprise but the sources do not address privileges for connected businesses.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred from mainstream Labour secular politics, the sources do not discuss denominational politics.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The sources do not address this idea; Brown's Britishness is values-based and forward-looking.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from mainstream Labour positions on gender equality, since the sources do not address divorce law.

national-resource-control.rationale: The sources show Brown favoured global cooperation and open trade, and give no view on national resource control.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Brownism pursues redistribution through tax credits and public spending, which implies outcome fairness matters; no source states the process-versus-outcome question.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred from Brown's calls for global financial regulation and cooperation in the 2008 UN speech; the sources do not mention this tax specifically.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred from mainstream Labour positions that discrimination remains a real obstacle; the sources do not address it.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Brownism is a pragmatic policy approach with no stated legal philosophy, and adherents' views would vary.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from Brown's emphasis on work, full employment and the New Deal as the route out of poverty; the sources do not discuss automation.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred from Brown's call for reformed international institutions and shared global governance in the 2008 UN speech.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred from Brown's market pragmatism; the sources do not discuss value theory.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Brownism couples a values-based Britishness with policies for working families such as tax credits and the minimum wage.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred from Brownism's focus on tax credits, jobs and public services over cultural questions; the sources do not frame the debate this way.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Brownism accepts markets but within a democratic social-democratic framework; the statement concerns a communist-party system the sources never address.

missingStatements.text: Governments should bind themselves to fiscal rules that allow borrowing only to invest over the economic cycle.
missingStatements.rationale: Brown legislated a golden rule and a debt ceiling as the core of his economic credibility, and Coyle describes the rule that borrowing is only for investment.

missingStatements.text: Governments should top up the incomes of low-paid working families through tax credits.
missingStatements.rationale: Coyle documents money going to low-paid working families through tax credits as a central redistributive tool of Brown's budgets.

notes: Sources conflict on whether Brownism is neoliberal or social democratic; Wikipedia records both readings. The audit follows the documented policy record. Primary-source coverage is limited to the 2008 UN speech, since full texts of Brown's other speeches could not be opened.
